name: How Do You Compare Kitchen Remodeling Contractor Bids?

mainEntity.name: How do I compare two kitchen renovation contractors who give very different prices?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare two kitchen renovation contractors who give very different prices?

acceptedAnswer.text: When two kitchen remodel bids are far apart, the first step is to compare line items. One contractor may be pricing a full scope with permits, inspections, disposal, and finish work, while another may be excluding those items or using low allowances for materials. In Los Angeles County, differences in permit handling, labor detail, and subcontractor pricing can also affect the total. Ask each contractor to confirm the exact scope in writing. You want to know whether the bid includes demolition, haul-away, rough plumbing, rough electrical, drywall repair, cabinet installation, countertop templating, backsplash tile, flooring transitions, painting, and final cleanup. Also check who is responsible for appliances, fixtures, and design support. A good comparison also looks at schedule, communication, warranty, and references, not only price. The lowest bid can become the most expensive if it leads to change orders, delays, or incomplete work. The best contractor is usually the one whose proposal is detailed, realistic, and consistent with the same project assumptions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare the scope, not just the total price. Check whether each contractor included permits, demolition, cabinets, finishes, appliances, plumbing, electrical, cleanup, and project management. Very different bids usually mean different assumptions, missing items, or different material allowances rather than a simple price gap.
